solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pluck shown by the French in a difficult situation

parts.note: to pluck a flower or fruit is to pick it
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Someone shows courage the French way while stuck in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' looks like a noun for courage, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a pickle is the idiom for being stuck in an awkward fix.

clue.text: It's easy to exert pressure directly above

parts.note: to push is to exert pressure on something
over means positioned directly above

explanation.surface: A physics tip: pressing straight down from above takes little effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is very easy to do or to beat is called a pushover, a noun idiom.

clue.text: Open letter about fellow seeking office

parts.note: candid means open, frank

indicators.note: about signals turning the Greek letter round so it reads backwards

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An open letter written about a man running for a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ETA, the Greek letter, into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person standing for election or applying for a post is a contender for that office.

clue.text: Ogle poet in recital

indicators.note: in recital means as spoken out loud, so we want a word sounding like the poet's name

parts.note: Edward Lear was the Victorian nonsense poet

explanation.surface: Someone eyes up a poet while reciting verse.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to look lecherously at someone, a near synonym.

clue.text: Removed from raised area as it's hidden from the audience

parts.note: off means removed, taken away
a stage is a raised platform

explanation.surface: Something taken down from a platform because the spectators cannot see it.
explanation.definitionFit: Action that happens in the wings of a theatre is out of the spectators' view.

clue.text: Deceitful practice in FE involving Midlands university

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the university goes inside the two letters

parts.note: FE is further education, as written
Aston University is in Birmingham, in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: Cheating in further education colleges implicating a Birmingham university.
explanation.walkthrough: FE is British shorthand for further education, colleges for students past school age.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling a fast one is the idiom for a sly trick or swindle.

clue.text: Very holy woman after bag with books concealing cocaine

indicators.note: after puts the woman's name behind the bag

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch
Rosa is a woman's name

indicators.note: concealing means the books hide the drug inside them

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: A pious woman caught with a bag of books hiding cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something regarded as too sacred to be violated is extremely holy.

clue.text: Love feeding greedy duck

indicators.note: feeding means going into, so the zero goes inside the eager word

parts.note: avid means eager, greedy
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone lovingly feeds a hungry duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is the verb, to dodge, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck something is to dodge or evade it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Complete with nationalist wearing English flag

indicators.note: wearing means the nationalist is dressed in, so sits inside, the other letters

parts.note: to flag is to tire, grow weary

explanation.surface: A nationalist draped in the English flag, outfit complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is the verb meaning to weaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete and whole are adjective synonyms for something with nothing missing.

clue.text: Having no doubt about the city being safe

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the certain word goes round the postcode

parts.note: sure means having no doubt
EC is the postal district of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone is confident that the city is a safe place.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Secure and safe are adjective synonyms for protected from danger.

clue.text: Foolish of London area head to accept extremely strange student

parts.note: SE is London's south-east postal area

indicators.note: to accept means the headland takes in the other letters

parts.note: a ness is a headland

indicators.note: extremely means take the extremes, the first and last letters of strange

parts.note: L is a learner, the student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A London head teacher foolishly admits a very odd student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland (NESS), not a person; 'to accept' puts SEL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Senseless means lacking good sense, so stupid or foolish.

clue.text: Look inside to switch off power

indicators.note: inside places the old word for look within the other word

parts.note: to cut the engine is to switch it off
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone peers in to turn off the electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power' is influence, not electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout is informal for influence or political weight.

clue.text: Sculptor's earliest cast of god

indicators.note: earliest cast means the first letter is thrown off

parts.note: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker

explanation.surface: The first casting of a god by a sculptor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' suggests bronze casting but means discarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief deity of Norse mythology.

clue.text: Unacceptable for detour to go wrong around Ohio

indicators.note: around means the mixed letters sit round the abbreviation
to go wrong means the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
O is the postal abbreviation for Ohio

explanation.surface: A road diversion in Ohio goes badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go wrong' mixes FOR DETOUR; 'around' wraps it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour beyond the rules or beyond the pale is improper and so unacceptable.

clue.text: Alcuin's first language embraced by head of historical territory

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside the word for head

parts.note: pate is an old word for head

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the scholar's name

parts.note: Latin is a language

explanation.surface: Alcuin, the medieval scholar, using Latin in a historic region.
explanation.definitionFit: A palatinate was a territory ruled by a count palatine, as in the Rhineland.

clue.text: Give out advance payment to cover article on space

indicators.note: on places the first part after the space

parts.note: an em is a printer's space

indicators.note: to cover means the stake goes over and around the article

parts.note: an ante is a stake paid in advance
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone pays a deposit to cover an article about outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space' is the printer's EM, not outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow from a source, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Pass by part of church with oddly neglected bell

indicators.note: oddly neglected means the odd letters are dropped and the even ones kept

parts.note: the apse is the curved end of a church

explanation.surface: A church with an unrung bell is passed by.
explanation.definitionFit: When time passes by it is said to go by or run out, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Odd fastener seen on clog

parts.note: a screw is a fastener
to ball is to clog, as snow balls up in a horse's hoof

explanation.surface: A strange fastening found on a wooden shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clog' looks like a shoe but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwball is an eccentric person, so used as an adjective it means crazy or peculiar.

clue.text: Set up in addition to protect separate gathering of drinkers

indicators.note: to protect means the reversed word wraps round the other
in a down clue set up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: yet means in addition, besides
apart means separate

explanation.surface: An event arranged to keep a drinking party apart from others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns YET into TEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea party is a social gathering where people drink tea.

clue.text: Happen to have unpleasant turn over unionist's smear

parts.note: to be is to happen, take place

indicators.note: over means the turned word sits over, covering, the unionist letter
turn means the word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: bad means unpleasant
U stands for unionist

explanation.surface: A unionist suffers a nasty turn and smears his opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses BAD to DAB.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedaub is to smear or plaster with something sticky.

clue.text: Bush and Blair at the outset lack organisation

indicators.note: at the outset means only the first letter of the name

parts.note: to ramble is to wander without plan or structure

explanation.surface: George Bush and Tony Blair were disorganised from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' and 'Blair' suggest the politicians; Bush is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bramble is a prickly shrub such as the blackberry.

clue.text: Soldiers caught in retreat trapped by river somewhere in Switzerland

indicators.note: trapped by means the reversed letters sit inside the river

parts.note: the Lune is a river in north-west England

indicators.note: in retreat means the letters go backwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Soldiers captured while retreating are cornered by a river in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is a Swiss city and lake, so a place in Switzerland.

clue.text: Essential to dismantle Antonio's shed

indicators.note: Essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Taking Antonio's shed apart is necessary.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed built against a wall.

clue.text: Appear to be heard describing King Charles as a funny guy

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so the sound-alike encloses the king
to be heard means we take a word with the same sound

parts.note: to seem is to appear
CR is Carolus Rex, King Charles

explanation.surface: Someone seems to have heard King Charles described as a comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A hilarious person is informally called a scream.

clue.text: Stop showing juggling act with Lily and Ada

indicators.note: juggling means the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A juggling act featuring Lily and Ada is being dropped from the show.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop work for the day or end an activity.

clue.text: Reveal impediment to Rona stripping off

parts.note: a let is an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'

indicators.note: stripping off means removing the outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: Rona's undressing is hindered.
explanation.definitionFit: To divulge a secret is a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Starts to worry about profits after opening of stock exchange

indicators.note: after puts the initials behind the opening letter
opening of means the first letter of stock
Starts to means the first letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: A trader begins to fret about profits after the stock exchange opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock exchange' reads as one phrase but splits: exchange is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade one thing for another is to make a straight exchange.

clue.text: Section on motorists laid up as a result of injury

indicators.note: laid up means set going upwards, so in a down clue the letters read backwards

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a motorists' organisation

explanation.surface: A group of motorists are bedridden after an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid up' hints at being ill in bed; here it reverses RAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark left on the skin after a wound heals is the lasting trace of an injury.

clue.text: Unusually without cunning in retrospect

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: art means cunning, craft

explanation.surface: Looking back, someone was oddly lacking in guile.
explanation.definitionFit: As an intensifier, as in extra large, the word means exceptionally.

clue.text: Hard to break absurd car habit with another means of transport

indicators.note: to break means the hard letter splits the mixed letters
absurd means the letters are put in a nonsensical order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, on pencils

explanation.surface: It's difficult to give up a silly driving habit for another way of travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' links to the car in the surface: this vehicle is pushed, not driven.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bath chair is a hooded wheelchair once used by invalids, so a way of getting about.

clue.text: Artificial intelligence ultimately occupying fellow geek

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: occupying means the letter sits inside the word for geek

parts.note: a nerd is a geek

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of intelligence

explanation.surface: AI takes over a nerdy man's life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artificial intelligence' reads as one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A mannered style is affected or stilted, so not natural.

clue.text: Outer portions of busby covering part said to provide elementary protection

indicators.note: covering means the outer letters wrap round the sound-alike
outer portions means the first and last letters of busby
said means we take a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A soldier's fur busby covers part of the head for basic protection.
explanation.walkthrough: A busby is a tall fur hat worn by British guardsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbrella shields you from the elements, the weather; brolly is British slang for it.
